title: Hindi: Devanagari Script

sources.name: Unicode Devanagari code chart; original explanations and examples

description: For beginners reading Hindi: vowels, consonants, nukta letters, vowel signs, conjuncts, digits, and useful words. Romanization uses macrons for long vowels; actual speech often drops inherent a.

cards.back: a; independent vowel, a short schwa-like sound.
ṛ; independent vowel, usually pronounced ri in modern Hindi.
ai; independent vowel, often pronounced like a long open e in standard Hindi.
au; independent vowel, often pronounced like a long open o in standard Hindi.
aṃ; a with anusvara, a nasal mark whose pronunciation depends on context.
aḥ; a with visarga, a breath-like sound found mainly in Sanskrit-derived forms.
ṅa; velar nasal consonant, like ng in sing; rare as an independent Hindi letter.
cards.example: अङ्ग (aṅg) — limb, Sanskrit-style spelling of अंग

cards.back: ña; palatal nasal consonant, mainly seen in conjuncts.
cards.example: पञ्च (pañc) — five, Sanskrit-style spelling of पंच

cards.back: tha; aspirated voiceless dental consonant, not the English th sound.
pha; aspirated voiceless bilabial consonant; often pronounced f in modern usage.
ya; consonant like English y in yes.
ra; consonant commonly realized as a tap or trill.
la; lateral consonant, similar to l.
va; consonant whose sound can fall between English v and w.
śa (sha); consonant similar to English sh.
ṣa; traditionally retroflex sh; usually merges with श in everyday Hindi.
qa; nukta form of क, used for q in loanwords; often pronounced k.
kha (kh as in German Bach); nukta form of ख representing a fricative.
gha (a voiced velar or uvular fricative); nukta form of ग.
za; nukta form of ज, representing z.
fa; nukta form of फ, representing f.
ṛa; nukta form of ड, a retroflex flap distinct from ऋ.
ṛha; nukta form of ढ, an aspirated retroflex flap.
kā; क plus the dependent vowel sign ा.
ki; क plus ि, written before the consonant but pronounced after it.
kī; क plus the dependent long i sign ी.
ku; क plus the dependent short u sign ु.
kū; क plus the dependent long u sign ू.
kṛ; क plus ृ, commonly pronounced kri in Hindi.
ke; क plus the dependent vowel sign े.
kai; क plus the dependent vowel sign ै.
ko; क plus the dependent vowel sign ो.
kau; क plus the dependent vowel sign ौ.
kṣa; conjunct of क् and ष, commonly pronounced ksh.
tra; conjunct of त् and र.
jña; conjunct of ज् and ञ, commonly pronounced gya in Hindi.
śra; conjunct of श् and र.

cards.example: नमस्ते, आप कैसे हैं? (namaste, āp kaise haĩ?) — Hello, how are you?
हाँ, मैं तैयार हूँ। (hā̃, maĩ taiyār hū̃.) — Yes, I am ready.
मुझे नहीं पता। (mujhe nahī̃ patā.) — I do not know.
मैं घर पर हूँ। (maĩ ghar par hū̃.) — I am at home.
आप कहाँ हैं? (āp kahā̃ haĩ?) — Where are you?
हम यहाँ हैं। (ham yahā̃ haĩ.) — We are here.

cards.back: yah; this; he, she, or it nearby (pronoun).
cards.example: यह मेरा घर है। (yah merā ghar hai.) — This is my house.

cards.back: vah; that; he, she, or it farther away (pronoun).
cards.example: वह मेरा मित्र है। (vah merā mitra hai.) — He is my friend.

cards.back: kyā; what; also marks a yes-no question.
cards.example: यह क्या है? (yah kyā hai?) — What is this?
घर कहाँ है? (ghar kahā̃ hai?) — Where is the house?
आप कब आएँगे? (āp kab āẽge?) — When will you come?
आप क्यों हँस रहे हैं? (āp kyõ hãs rahe haĩ?) — Why are you laughing?

cards.back: kaise; how (adverb); masculine plural or respectful form of कैसा.
cards.example: आप कैसे हैं? (āp kaise haĩ?) — How are you?
मेरा घर छोटा है। (merā ghar choṭā hai.) — My house is small.
मुझे पानी चाहिए। (mujhe pānī cāhie.) — I want water.
चाय गरम है। (cāy garam hai.) — The tea is hot.
यह मेरी किताब है। (yah merī kitāb hai.) — This is my book.
आज अच्छा दिन है। (āj acchā din hai.) — Today is a good day.
रात हो गई। (rāt ho gaī.) — Night has fallen.
आज छुट्टी है। (āj chuṭṭī hai.) — Today is a holiday.

cards.back: kal; yesterday or tomorrow, determined by context (adverb).
cards.example: कल मिलेंगे। (kal milẽge.) — We will meet tomorrow.
यह अच्छा है। (yah acchā hai.) — This is good.

cards.back: dhanyavād; thanks (masculine noun, used as an expression).
cards.example: आपकी मदद के लिए धन्यवाद। (āpkī madad ke lie dhanyavād.) — Thank you for your help.
